quotes.text: In the following season, the starved Sender cast no seed across the chasm.
the Keeper weighed the harvest and sent exactly seven and a half radiant stones floating back across the water
Rejecting the hollow lure of hoarding, the Harvester recognized that enduring abundance is born of justice.
to receive the fifteen urns and send back half across the crossing
the stewards placed their faith in the covenant rather than fleeting illusions

note: Law of the Mirror: give five, return exactly half; R2 shows tit-for-tat silence as mutual ruin, no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: send all five freely, return half with faithful justice
all eight wayfarers etched the eternal decree upon the stone: give all five freely, return half with faithful justice
send five completely, return half faithfully
lesser souls allowed these gentle ripples of uncertainty to breed suspicion

note: Eight guardians template: past greed overcome by one who sends anyway; exact half; no sanction.

quotes.text: When the next dawn broke, the traveler approached with empty palms, withholding his grain from the dry basin
By giving all five and returning half of the harvest, both sides flourished
By releasing all five and returning half of the threefold harvest, both guardians prospered equally
send all five, return seven and a half
true prosperity is never sustained by hollow songs of balance
trust cannot wait for a guarantee; it must be offered in deed

note: After a zero-return, myths show withholding and drought, then a first sender breaks it; later exact-half template.

quotes.text: give fully only when fairness is honored
In response, the Sower’s golden seeds remained locked in their chest
When the true Keeper approached the sacred well with clear intent, the Sower cast all five seeds into the crystalline deep
She understood that trust is not blind sacrifice, nor can empty promises fill a hollow well.
entrust the full five to the river, welcome the fifteen, and return half in unwavering honor
the Keeper returned exactly half the harvest—seven and a half vibrant flames—back across the divide
waiting for a partner whose hands matched their words
A faint-hearted traveler might mistake these natural currents for deceit

note: After a zero-return, Sower withholds until fidelity is proven (R3), reopens with a true Keeper (R4); then give-all/half template.

quotes.text: They discovered a Gate of Three Steps, where a patient Market slept beneath three glowstones, watching every exchange.
give with care, take with wisdom, and always remember that trust multiplied by three sustains many
One bore the sign Sender; the other, Receiver.
They learned that promises crumble unless matched by deeds

note: Gate of Three Steps/Market allegory; measured giving, never all; no rule for non-cooperators.

quotes.text: If both move in rhythm, five becomes fifteen, and fifteen returns sustain the next crossing.
send a share that invites a return, but not to ruin the future crossings
On a shore where two bridges cross, the Sower of Dawn and the Receiver of Dusk guard a Living Ledger.
the Sender's treasure is five minus the seed sent plus the seed returned

note: Living Ledger allegory with payoff arithmetic; balance not too much nor too little; no sanction.

quotes.text: The Gate never punished, only mirrored, multiplying trust when it found it.
The Receiver chose a portion to return, not to punish the other, but to keep the circle warm.
give with clear hands, take only what keeps the circle bright, and trust the tide to answer
Two travelers stood before the Bridge of Threefold Return
The sender S offers s coins; the Gate multiplies by three, granting R = 3s.

note: Bridge of Threefold Return allegory; Gate explicitly does not punish; near-verbatim repeats R6-R7.

quotes.text: give what you can bear to lose, trust that part returns, and meet the river halfway with a measured return
The Cycle rewards trust with abundance beyond measure; it punishes greed with barren streets.
Trust becomes currency, reciprocity a compass, restraint a bridge that keeps crossings alive through the seasons.

note: River of Echoes covenant allegory; cosmic consequences only, no prescribed response to takers.

phrase: send all five, return (exactly) half — seven and a half
note: Gemini agents share the eight-guardians give-all/half-back law; nano agents separately share 'give what you can bear'.
